visual_action: A basketball travels through the White House in a POV/first-person style sequence. Scene 1: The ball bounces across the South Lawn toward the White House South Portico, with the American flag flying above. Scene 2: The ball approaches a White House exterior door at night/dusk, framed by white columns and a bare tree. Scene 3: Inside the White House foyer/entrance hall, a Marine in dress uniform salutes as the ball flies past; two framed presidential photographs hang on the wall behind him (one showing two figures standing on a stage, another appearing to show a figure at a podium). Scene 4: The ball bounces/rolls down a sunlit White House colonnade corridor (West Colonnade), with gold decorative elements and framed plaques/items on the right wall. Scene 5: Close-up of two gold-framed items on the wall — one showing the Duke Blue Devils basketball logo (partial "D" with basketball) and one showing the Florida Gators logo (green gator in orange circle). Scene 6: The ball rolls down the same colonnade corridor toward double doors labeled "West Wing." Scene 7: The ball bounces along another White House colonnade, past white chairs and a table visible at the far end. Scene 8: Close-up of a Wilson EVO NXT official NCAA March Madness basketball, slowly rotating, well-lit against a dark background.

intended_effect: Entertain and delight viewers with a fun, behind-the-scenes-style White House March Madness promotion; generate engagement and shareability around NCAA tournament season.
uncertainty_flags: The two framed photographs in the White House foyer/entrance hall behind the Marine are partially visible — one appears to show two male figures on a stage and the other a figure at a podium, but faces/identities are not clearly discernible from the keyframe.
The gold-framed team logos on the colonnade wall appear to be a bracket/picks display; other team logos beyond Duke and Florida Gators may be present but are not legible in the available frames.
It is unclear whether the colonnade display of team logos represents an official White House March Madness bracket or is set-dressing for the video.

Whether this was filmed entirely on-location at the actual White House or partly on a replica/set cannot be confirmed from frames alone, though the account is @whitehouse and details appear consistent with the real building.
